citation.note: Wage record retention (NDCC § 34-14-04): System must retain promotion records (wage change, effective date, justification) for minimum 2 years; support Department of Labor inspection rights.
Pay frequency: Regular paydays required; semimonthly or monthly common; must be consistent and predictable (NDCC § 34-14-02).

Final pay on separation during/after promotion (NDCC § 34-14-03): If termination occurs post-promotion, ensure all wages earned at promoted rate from effective date forward are paid by next regular payday or within 15 days of separation, whichever first; unused accrued leave is paid unless the narrow at-hire/tenure/notice exception is met (NDCC § 34-14-03).

citation.note: Post-employment non-competes and non-solicits void except business-sale/partnership-dissolution contexts; on promotion mark any employee covenant unenforceable (NDCC § 9-08-06).

body.rule: Post-employment non-competes and non-solicits void except business-sale/partnership-dissolution contexts; on promotion mark any employee covenant unenforceable (NDCC § 9-08-06).

citation.note: North Dakota tracks the federal floor; verify wage meets $7.25/hour on promotion or base-pay change.

Equal Pay compliance (NDCC § 34-06.1): On promotion or base-pay change within same establishment, system should flag if new wage for one gender differs materially from peer rates for comparable work; require manager justification or HR approval for outlier increases.

Whistleblower protection check (NDCC § 34-01-20): if promotion follows a good-faith report of unlawful conduct, flag for legal review. Lawful off-duty activities protected unless conflicting with essential business interests (NDCC § 14-02.4).

No comprehensive drug-testing statute; broad discretion (pre-employment, reasonable-suspicion, post-accident, random); the employer pays for required tests and records; written policy recommended (NDCC § 34-11.1).
Notice in the most expedient manner possible and without unreasonable delay; Attorney General notice if 250+ residents affected; encryption safe harbor; up to $5,000 per violation (NDCC § 51-30).
